description: Generating the subject and then referencing it. The first step draws a character with Z-Image and the second conditions MiniMax-H3's 'ref2va' on it, with 'from_previous_result' naming the step whose output the reference is built from instead of a file on disk - so nothing is written out and read back, and the whole thing is one workflow rather than two runs. An image reference takes the picture as it is; a video reference built the same way brings the frames and the soundtrack generated with them. 'release_pipeline' frees the drawing pipeline before the video model loads, since the two never need the device at once.
summary: H3 video of a character Z-Image draws first, referenced in-workflow rather than from a file.

vram_estimate.reason: Ref2VA holds every reference's encoding resident beside the video latents, so the ceiling is a fixed base, a per-voxel term for the VAE decode's conv3d activation (width * height * num_frames), and a per-reference term. Classified against the 24 GB entry from the #479 field report (lem, RTX 3090 24 GB, int4 + 768p turbo LoRA, 9 steps, 2026-09-25/26) at 1344x768: 175 frames x 2 refs, 209 x 2 and 175 x 3 ran (projected 22.83, 23.77 and 23.83 GB); 209 x 3 OOM'd in reference encode needing a further 5.1 GB and 260 x 1 OOM'd at denoise step 1 needing a further 4.8 GB (projected 24.77 and 24.18 GB). The refused allocations are lower bounds, not peaks, so this is a classification with about 0.2 GB of margin either side, not a fitted curve. bytes_per_voxel is unchanged from #324's calibration (job 282172105da1); base_gb drops 0.3 GB now the references are counted separately

variables.prompt:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the deep-sea diver in <Picture 1>, in a heavy canvas suit and a brass helmet with the faceplate open, whose face, helmet, suit and proportions define their appearance for the whole video.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video shows <Subject 1> speaking directly to camera in the setting of <Picture 1>, in one continuous take.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the face, helmet, suit and proportions of <Picture 1> are kept exactly, with the head, jaw and shoulders newly animated to speak.

detailed_description:
The target video is in realistic photographic style. [Shot 1] A medium close-up frames <Subject 1> from the chest up, centred and facing camera in the setting of <Picture 1>, held as one continuous shot. The lighting of <Picture 1> is kept exactly as it is, the warm rim light steady along the brass of the helmet and the background staying dark and well behind in shallow focus. <Subject 1> (S1), a low and gravelled male voice, unhurried and worn, says <d>[English] Down there the light gives out first. Everything else follows.</d> The jaw and lips move in natural synchronisation with the speech and settle closed at the end of the line. Between phrases <Subject 1> shifts weight very slightly and the head drifts a few degrees off centre and back, with the eyes staying on the lens and blinking at a natural rate. The camera holds a static shot throughout.

overall_soundscape:
A quiet, close room tone at an even level from the first frame to the last, with a faint creak of canvas as <Subject 1> shifts weight and a single soft knock of a glove against the brass collar.

non_diegetic_music:
N/A

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
